title: UserHasSubscription ignores STRIPE_ENABLED=false (pro features locked server-side)
description:
Commit 0eb045e2 'Add STRIPE_ENABLED off-switch' wired StripeConfig into the Handler and made billing routes 404 + frontend unlock pro, but the backend gate was missed.

ProcessCardAfterCreation (handlers/cards.go:1336) calls Handler.UserHasSubscription (handlers/users.go:736), which returns services.UserHasSubscription (services/subscription.go) = stripe_subscription_status in (active, trialing). With STRIPE_ENABLED=false nobody ever gets an active status, so entity/fact extraction after card creation is silently skipped on every billing-less self-host, even though the frontend treats everyone as subscribed.

Fix: Handler.UserHasSubscription should return true when !s.StripeConfig.Enabled (mirror the frontend AuthContext logic). Add a test: STRIPE_ENABLED=false + user with 'free' status + card creation -> ProcessEntitiesAndFacts runs.
acceptance_criteria: With STRIPE_ENABLED=false, card creation processes entities/facts for users with no Stripe status; with billing enabled, behavior unchanged.
close_reason: Handler.UserHasSubscription returns true when StripeConfig.Enabled==false; services.UserHasSubscription unchanged as raw Stripe check. Tests: TestUserHasSubscriptionHonorsBillingSwitch. Landed 229e056d.

title: Bootstrap first admin on fresh self-host install
description:
On a brand-new instance, NO user can ever become admin, which makes the /admin UI and all admin-only routes unusable.

Evidence: users.is_admin defaults to false (schema.sqlite.sql:908); the only place that sets is_admin in production code is none (tests do it directly via SQL, tests/conftest.go:436); UpdateUserRoute (handlers/users.go:121) blocks non-admins from changing admin status; GitHub/OIDC flows never assign is_admin.

SaaS worked because the operator already had an admin account; a fresh self-host starts with zero admins and no promotion path.

Proposed fix (pick one or combine):
- First registered user becomes admin (guarded so it only happens once).
- Auto-promote the user whose email matches ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL (or a new ADMIN_EMAILS env var) on registration/OIDC provisioning.
- CLI/flag bootstrap (e.g. zg admin promote <email>) as a backstop.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh SQLite DB + first registered user yields an admin; existing installs unaffected; covered by a test.
close_reason: CreateUser now makes the first user on an empty install admin, plus ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL match (case-insensitive). Tests: TestCreateUserFirstUserBecomesAdmin, TestCreateUserAdminEmailGrantsAdmin. Landed 229e056d.

title: Convert python-mail service to Go (embed SMTP in backend)
description:
Goal: eliminate the separate Flask mailer (python-mail/) so self-hosting is one Go binary + SQLite (fewer services to run, one language, no ZETTEL_MAIL_* env duplication).

Current architecture:
- go-backend/mail.MailClient (mail/mail.go) POSTs JSON to m.Host + '/api/send' with Authorization: m.Password — the python service does the actual SMTP.
- python-mail/app.py exposes /api/send, /api/send/mailing-list, /health; hard-crashes at boot without ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER/USERNAME/PASSWORD/DEFAULT_SENDER.
- docker-compose.yml always deploys mail-service (python image) on :8081; MAIL_HOST=localhost / MAIL_PASSWORD are the Go side's pointer into it.

Plan:
- Replace the HTTP hop with direct SMTP in Go (net/smtp or a maintained lib; keep the existing MailClient API/queue so callers don't change).
- Keep or fold the mailing-list email path (see mailing-list removal bead — if that lands first, /api/send/mailing-list dies with it).
- Remove python-mail/, its Dockerfile, the compose mail-service, and the ZETTEL_MAIL_* / MAIL_HOST / MAIL_PASSWORD wiring.
- Coordinate with 6er.6 (mail optional): MAIL_ENABLED=false + auto-validate email becomes the no-mail self-host path.

Acceptance: docker compose up runs without the mail-service container; transactional email (validation, password reset, reminders) is sent by the Go backend directly; python-mail/ deleted.
acceptance_criteria: docker compose up runs without the mail-service container; transactional email is sent by the Go backend directly; python-mail/ deleted.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (2026-08-07 audit of python-mail):

WHAT THE PYTHON SERVICE DOES (python-mail/app.py):
1. POST /api/send — one transactional email: subject/recipient/body/is_html; sender ('Zettelgarden', DEFAULT_SENDER); 400 if no subject/recipient, 500 on SMTP failure.
2. POST /api/send/mailing-list — TO + BCC lists. DEAD CODE from the Go backend's perspective: SendMailingListMessage (mail/mailing_list.go) loops per-recipient via SendHTMLEmail and never hits this endpoint. Dies with 6er.11.
3. GET /health — no-op in-process.
SMTP: ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER, port 587 default, MAIL_USE_TLS=True (STARTTLS), username/password auth, DEFAULT_SENDER. File logging (ZETTEL_MAIL_LOG).

GO PORT SCOPE:
1. SMTP transport — net/smtp is insufficient (built-in auth only PLAIN/CRAM-MD5, no implicit TLS, no MIME, no RFC 2047, no timeouts). Use a maintained lib (github.com/go-mail/mail or wneessen/go-mail) to mirror Flask-Mail: STARTTLS 587 + implicit TLS 465, PLAIN/LOGIN auth, dial/send timeouts so a dead SMTP server can't wedge the queue.
2. MIME construction: From ('Zettelgarden <from@...>'), To, Subject RFC 2047-encoded (welcome subject has emoji: 'Welcome to Zettelgarden! 🌱'), Date, MIME-Version, text/plain vs text/html (gomarkdown HTML bodies), UTF-8 Content-Transfer-Encoding.
3. Config consolidation: merge MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PASSWORD (Go) + ZETTEL_MAIL_SERVER/USERNAME/PASSWORD/DEFAULT_SENDER (python) into one set: host:port, username, password, from, TLS mode. Fold in 6er.6 semantics (unset = disabled, no crash, no banner nag via auto-validate).
4. Update all MailClient constructions: main.go:163, cmd/reminders/main.go:19, tests/conftest.go:224. Keep queue/retry(4x,1s)/shutdown-drain/Testing-bypass in mail/mail.go unchanged — only sendMailImpl swaps HTTP POST -> SMTP.
5. Deployment cleanup: delete python-mail/, drop mail-service from both compose files (stops build.sh building it), replace ZETTEL_MAIL_* docs in .env.example with consolidated block.

SEQUENCING: do WITH 6er.11 (mailing-list removal deletes SendMailingListMessage/SendWelcomeEmail/HandleAddToMailingList -> only single-recipient path remains) and AFTER/ALONGSIDE 6er.6 (mail optional). Suggested order: 6er.11 first, then 6er.12+6er.6 as one change touching the mail surface once.
IMPLEMENTED in branch zg-6er12 (commit 4b410a30, pushed to origin, not yet merged to master — merge blocked by concurrent agents on the shared tree; only README.md expected conflict).

Summary: wneessen/go-mail v0.8.1; MailClient sendMailImpl delivers directly over SMTP (STARTTLS default, implicit TLS 465, plain when SMTP_STARTTLS=false; 10s dial/30s send timeouts; PLAIN auth when creds present; RFC 2047 + HTML handled by lib). Config MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PASSWORD -> SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD/SMTP_FROM/SMTP_STARTTLS; MAIL_ENABLED auto-detect preserved; prod validation requires SMTP_HOST+SMTP_FROM when enabled. Fake in-process SMTP server tests (plain/HTML+emoji/AUTH/STARTTLS); fixed pre-existing Shutdown data race (-race clean). python-mail/ deleted; compose mail-service removed; env examples rewritten; README/AGENTS/CLAUDE updated; mailing_list.go untouched (6er.11 still pending). Verified: go test ./... green, tsc green. TO MERGE: git merge origin/zg-6er12 (needs quiet tree), then close.
close_reason: Merged to master as 1f09617f (merge of zg-6er12). Direct SMTP in Go (wneessen/go-mail v0.8.1): STARTTLS default, implicit TLS 465, plain when SMTP_STARTTLS=false; 10s/30s timeouts; PLAIN auth when creds set; RFC 2047 + HTML via lib. Config MAIL_HOST/MAIL_PASSWORD -> SMTP_* with MAIL_ENABLED auto-detect preserved. title: Phase 6a: replace Postgres '~' regex in GetNextRootCardID (cards.go) — missed Phase 3 PG-ism
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Phase 3's PG-ism inventory checked ARRAY[ and = ANY($1) but NOT the Postgres regex match operator '~'. Two call sites survive:

- services/cards.go:810 — GetNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
- handlers/cards.go:494 — (s *Handler) getNextRootCardID: AND card_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'

SQLite has no '~' regex operator (REGEXP requires a user-defined function). The query errors silently, returns empty, and GetNextRootCardID falls back to '1' instead of the correct MAX(numeric)+1. This breaks 3 handler tests (TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute, contributes to TestGetNextChildCardID) and is a REAL production bug post-cutover: every new root card would collide on id '1'.

Note these are duplicate implementations (services + handlers both inline the SQL). The handlers copy is the legacy dup; services.GetNextRootCardID is the canonical one (called from handlers/epub.go).

Fix: no cross-driver SQL expresses 'pure digits' (LIKE has no char classes on either DB; GLOB is SQLite-only). Pull the filter into Go: SELECT candidate card_id WHERE user_id/is_deleted, then filter with regexp.MustCompile('^[0-9]+$').MatchString and take the max via strconv.Atoi. At single-user scale this is trivial. Ideally dedupe the two impls onto the services one and have the handler call it.

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Blocks the cards-id cluster of Zettelgarden-j89.
acceptance_criteria: GetNextRootCardID works identically on Postgres and SQLite; the '~' operator is gone from services/cards.go and handlers/cards.go; TestGetNextRootCardID, TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; no other PG regex operators remain in non-test Go (grep clean).
close_reason: Fixed in de7b122e. services.GetNextRootCardID now filters pure-numeric ids in Go (regexp) — no '~' operator remains in non-test Go (grep clean). Deduped the handler copy onto it. TestGetNextRootCardID + TestGetNextRootCardIDRoute green on SQLite; full services/server/models/routes packages still green; handlers failures 11 -> 9.

title: Remove test-quality landmines: global fetch mock, act() warnings, mocking strategy
description:
Why: the current test setup quietly produces false confidence. (1) src/tests/setup.ts installs a GLOBAL fetch mock that returns {} for every unmatched request — a component whose API wiring is broken still passes because every endpoint "succeeds" with an empty object. title: Phase 1b: headless two-DB convergence harness
description:
No-UI harness validating the engine through a live backend (design: Phase 1 exit criteria + second/third-pass review items). Two local DBs + live backend.

Scenarios (each must converge both DBs to identical content matching the server):
- Offline gaps: device A edits while offline, device B edits, both sync.
- Concurrent edits: LWW resolves deterministically; lost-edit count reported.
- Offline-created linked rows: card created offline on A; task created offline on B linked via tasks.card_pk; same-named tag created offline on BOTH devices → one server tag, both device references remapped to it.
- Offline card_id rename on both devices → must not split one logical row.
- Interleaved push/pull: a device's own echoed changes are not double-applied.
- Tag rename-vs-create and rename-vs-rename per the v1 policy (LWW on merged row; renamed-away name soft-deleted).
acceptance_criteria: Harness exits non-zero on any divergence; all scenarios above converge; runnable headless (no UI) as a CI step.

title: Phase 1a: shared TS sync engine core
description:
Shared TypeScript sync library (design: Shared Sync Engine). Transport-agnostic; consumed by desktop and mobile; team's language.

- StorageAdapter interface (get/put/delete/query) + SQLite implementation. IndexedDB adapter deferred (web enhancement, Phase 4).
- Local mirror: the three pinned tables (+ junction tables read-only) in local SQLite.
- Outbox: every local mutation writes local row + queued change (collection, row_uuid, op, base_version) in one tx. row_uuid = idempotency key; base_version = concurrency check.
- Bootstrap + pull: first sync = snapshot; thereafter changes?since=<cursor>; apply, advance cursor.
- Push: drain outbox via /sync/push; apply server mapping (row_uuid → PK rewrite of local refs); tags: adopt merged server sync_uuid locally (losing device rewrites its own tag row).
- Reconcile: LWW by (version, updated_at, device_id); junctions pull-only overwrite (never merge); lost-edit count surfaced.
- Self-echo rule: after push, the feed echoes the client's own changes — mark outbox entries confirmed before applying the feed (or dedupe by row_uuid+version) so own writes aren't re-applied/double-bumped.
- Sync scheduler: online/offline detection, exponential backoff, periodic pull, progress events (lastSynced, pendingChanges).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests green against the SQLite adapter; outbox survives offline gaps; retries idempotent; self-echo does not double-apply own changes; cursor advances correctly across snapshot→incremental transition.
close_reason: Phase 1a complete: shared TS sync engine (sync-engine/). StorageAdapter contract (InMemory + better-sqlite3 impls), HttpTransport, SyncEngine core: local-first mutate/deleteLocal (atomic mirror+outbox), bootstrap via snapshot, pull (never clobbers pending rows, advances cursor), push (drains outbox, applies server mappings: id/version adoption, conflict reconciliation to server row, tag merge adoption of surviving uuid + server data), self-echo idempotent, concurrent sync() shares in-flight promise, scheduler with online/offline + exponential backoff + progress events. Also fixed API contract: changes feed now carries collection (was missing); tag merge responses now include server row data. 16 vitest tests green (adapter tx/coalesce + 11 engine scenarios incl. two-device convergence, dropped-response retry, offline gap, cross-device conflict). title: Phase 0b: sync API (snapshot, changes feed, push) + exit-criteria script
description:
Sync endpoints (design: Backend Work 3-5, 8). Per-user scoped, additive, nothing existing changes.

- GET /api/sync/snapshot?collections=… — full current state per collection. Bootstrap: sync_log starts empty at migration time, so new devices pull snapshot at cursor 0 then incremental. Also solves reinstalls.
- GET /api/sync/changes?since=<cursor>&collections=… — incremental feed ordered by sync_log.id; cursor = per-user max seen id, not contiguous.
- POST /api/sync/push — transactional batch upsert/delete. Each change: row_uuid (idempotency key — retry replays same op) + base_version (concurrency check). Resolves row_uuid → server int PK in-tx covering EVERY FK on the pinned tables: cards.parent_id, tasks.card_pk (offline task attached to offline card = common case), tasks.parent_task_id; returns the mapping so the client rewrites local references.
- Tags merge BY NAME (tags(name) has no UNIQUE constraint; CreateTag reuses (user_id,name) incl. deleted, resurrecting it): find (user_id,name) incl. deleted → reuse, else create; return merged row's sync_uuid/id so the losing device adopts the winner's uuid locally (or next push re-creates a duplicate). Same-name tag from two devices = ONE server row, both remapped.
- Parent relationships server-authoritative: server derives parent_id from card_id on push (UpdateCard already does this via DiscoverParentId); client never sends parent_id; offline-created cards stay roots.
- Optimistic concurrency: stale base_version → LWW by (version, updated_at, device_id tie-breaker) or conflict-reject for deletes; lost-edit count returned.

Exit-criteria script (also the acceptance exercise): snapshot-bootstrap an empty client; pull feed; push batch incl. offline-created card + task linked via card_pk + same-named tag from two devices (must merge to one row, both remapped); idempotent retry produces no duplicates; stale base_version rejected/LWW deterministic; rename-vs-create tag case per policy.
acceptance_criteria: Exit-criteria script from the description passes end-to-end against a live backend; idempotent retries produce no duplicate rows; tag name-merge yields one row with both device references remapped; stale base_version pushes are LWW-resolved or rejected deterministically; tasks.card_pk and tasks.parent_task_id and cards.parent_id all resolve for offline-created rows. Go tests green.

title: Migrate admin config to an app-managed config file with admin UI (instead of env vars)
description:
Admin-facing configuration currently lives in env vars (ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL, MAIL_*, SIGNUPS_ENABLED etc.), which a self-hoster must edit and restart the service to change. For a purely self-hosted app, admin settings should be manageable in-app via the /admin UI.

Chosen approach (see design): a single app-managed YAML config file (./data/config.yaml) as the source of truth for non-secret admin settings, seeded from env on first boot, with hot reload (mtime-checked cache) so UI edits apply without restart. Secrets and boot-time infra stay in env. Zero DB schema changes.

Surfaces being migrated:
- ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL (pkg/config/server.go:25) — notification recipient (handlers/billing.go:178) becomes admin_email.
- Future admin-tunable settings from sibling beads: SIGNUPS_ENABLED (6er.10), MAIL_ENABLED / EMAIL_AUTO_VALIDATE (6er.6), support email (6er.7), site name.

Scope boundary: this bead covers admin-managed non-secret app config (admin email, site name, registration toggle, mail toggle, support email). It does NOT move secrets (Stripe/mail/Typesense/LLM credentials, SECRET_KEY, OAuth secrets) or boot-time infra (ZETTEL_PORT, ZETTEL_URL, SQLITE_PATH, STORAGE_DIR) into the file — those stay in env/config.
design:
Design (2026-08-07) — config-file approach (Gitea/Matomo style), replacing the earlier DB-backed draft.

## Decision summary
- Admin-tunable, non-secret settings live in ONE YAML file: ./data/config.yaml (next to SQLite).
- The file is the single source of truth for those settings; env vars only SEED it on first boot.
- Env retains: secrets (SECRET_KEY, MAIL_PASSWORD, STRIPE_*, TYPESENSE_PASSWORD, ZETTEL_LLM_KEY, OAuth client secrets) + boot infra (ZETTEL_PORT, ZETTEL_URL, SQLITE_PATH, STORAGE_DIR).
- Admin UI reads/writes the file via admin API; hand-edits are supported (file is the real store).
- HOT RELOAD: settings service caches the file, checks mtime on read, invalidates on change; UI saves update the cache directly. No restart needed. No new dependencies (yaml.v3 already in go.mod; no fsnotify).
- Zero DB schema changes (no app_settings table, no self-heal work, no migration story).

## Settings file shape
```yaml
# Admin-managed settings. Managed via the admin UI; edit by hand at your own risk.
admin_email: admin@example.com
site_name: Zettelgarden
signups_enabled: true
mail_enabled: true
email_auto_validate: true
support_email: admin@example.com
```
Keys + env seed sources:
- admin_email         <- ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL     (string; validated contains @)
- site_name           <- ZETTEL_SITE_NAME       (new; default "Zettelgarden")
- signups_enabled     <- SIGNUPS_ENABLED        (bool; default true)   [coordinate 6er.10]
- mail_enabled        <- MAIL_ENABLED           (bool; auto-detect from MAIL_HOST) [coordinate 6er.6]
- email_auto_validate <- EMAIL_AUTO_VALIDATE    (bool; default true when billing off) [6er.6]
- support_email       <- ZETTEL_SUPPORT_EMAIL   (string) [coordinate 6er.7]

## Boot & resolution
1. LoadConfig() from env unchanged (validation still runs; secrets/boot-infra only).
2. If ./data/config.yaml missing: write it seeded from env-derived defaults (atomic temp+rename), log "created settings file seeded from env".
3. SettingsService loads file into an in-memory map (key -> typed value), timestamped with file mtime.
4. Every Get/GetBool: stat file; if mtime changed, reload. (File is tiny; stat is cheap.)
5. Effective value = file value. Env is ignored for these keys after first boot. One-sentence rule: the file is the only place admin settings change after first boot; env seeds it once.
6. Invalid/hand-broken YAML: fail loudly at boot (clear message pointing at the file); UI never overwrites a file it failed to parse.

## Backend access
- New settings package (e.g. go-backend/settings or services/settings.go): Load, Get, GetBool, Set, All, path resolution.
  - Settings path: derive from data dir (default ./data/config.yaml; override via ZETTEL_CONFIG_FILE if we want an escape hatch).
  - Set(): validate value against key type, write atomic temp+rename under mutex, update cache immediately.
- Replace direct env reads: handlers/billing.go:178 (ZETTEL_ADMIN_EMAIL) -> settings.Get("admin_email"). New toggles (signups, mail) read through the settings service.
- Public GET /api/settings (like billing-status): returns ONLY non-secret keys (all keys in this file are non-secret by construction) so the frontend reacts at runtime without VITE_* rebuilds.
- Admin GET /api/admin/settings (admin-only): current values. PUT /api/admin/settings (admin-only): partial update (subset of keys), validates, writes file atomically, LogAdminAction audit with before/after in details.

## Admin UI
- New /admin/settings page: form per key (text input / toggle / save), loaded from GET /api/admin/settings, saved via PUT /api/admin/settings. Shows "applied immediately" (hot reload).
- Sidebar entry in AdminPage.tsx.
- Optionally a read-only "managed via env" section listing secrets/boot-infra keys for discoverability.

## Frontend runtime consumption
- Add getSettings() to src/api; AuthContext (or a SettingsContext) fetches public /api/settings once and exposes site_name, signups_enabled, mail_enabled, email_auto_validate, support_email.
- Consume: hide register link when signups disabled; hide email-validation banner when mail off; use support_email in UserSettings instead of hardcoded info@zettelgarden.com (6er.7); site_name in document title.

## Phasing
1. settings package + config.yaml seed-on-first-boot + migrate admin_email reads (no UI). Boot test: file created, values correct; hot-reload test: touch file, value changes.
2. Public GET /api/settings; frontend consumes the five values at runtime.
3. Admin GET/PUT /api/admin/settings + /admin/settings page.
4. Flip new toggles to settings-backed (6er.10 signups, 6er.6 mail) and update root .env.example (6er.1) to document that these are file-managed now.

## Open questions (small)
- Escape hatch var ZETTEL_CONFIG_FILE (default ./data/config.yaml) — include or hardcode the default path?
- Should site_name/support_email stay VITE_-driven on the frontend for now, or fully runtime via /api/settings? (Proposal: runtime; VITE_* only for things that genuinely must be build-time.)
acceptance_criteria: An admin can change the in-app admin settings from the /admin UI and they persist in SQLite across restarts; env vars still seed defaults on first boot; secrets remain in the config file.

description: Code-review finding surfaced by the OIDC work (Zettelgarden-0ck) but pre-existing and broader. findOrCreateOIDCUser, the GitHub OAuth path (oauth.go), and the password CreateUser path all do existence-check-then-INSERT against the pool with no transaction. OIDC adds another vector on top of GitHub/password. Decision needed: is email globally unique by product rule? If yes, add a unique index (migration 0148) and handle the constraint violation as a clean 'email already exists' error rather than relying on the check-then-insert window. ## Part 1 — Cutover procedure (operational; ~30 min downtime)
Follow the Cutover Runbook in the design doc. Iterate against a COPY only; the final run is against the now-static live Postgres.
1. Stop the app (set read-only or halt the go_backend container).
2. Final insurance: `pg_dump -Fc zg_internal > zg_internal_dump-cutover-$(date +%Y%m%d).dump` — store off-host, keep ≥90 days. (Prior insurance dump from gate 1: /home/nick/zg_internal_dump-20260728-124426.dump, 111 MB.)
3. Build the ETL: `cd go-backend && go build -o migrate-pg-to-sqlite ./cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite`.
4. Run the final import against a fresh SQLite file: `./migrate-pg-to-sqlite --pg-dsn '<live DSN>' --sqlite-path ./data/zettelgarden.db`
5. Verification gates (do not proceed unless all green): per-table COUNT(*) PG==SQLite exact; `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` clean; `PRAGMA integrity_check` ok; spot-check a few cards' body md5 + sub-graphs.
6. Flip config: `DB_DRIVER=sqlite`, `SQLITE_PATH=/app/data/zettelgarden.db`. Restart go_backend.
7. Smoke-test in prod: dashboard counts, a card detail, task list, chat history, create+edit a card.

## Part 2 — Code/config cleanup (lands with the flip)
- [ ] Remove the `db` (postgres:16-alpine) service from docker-zettel-run.yml + its `depends_on: service_healthy` on go_backend; mount the SQLite data dir instead.
- [ ] go-backend/.env.example: replace DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/NAME with `DB_DRIVER=sqlite` + `SQLITE_PATH=./data/zettelgarden.db`.

- [ ] scripts/addParentId.go + scripts/computeKeywords.go: both are `//go:build ignore` one-shots; computeKeywords.go is already obsolete (references deleted llms.ComputeCardKeywords). Decide: archive both, or port to the driver abstraction. Recommend archive (they write none of the trigger-affected tables; re-run need is nil post-cutover).
- [ ] Update README.md self-hosting section (lines 62/89/97/100/125 — drop "PostgreSQL + pgvector"; "no external database"). Update AGENTS.md project note (line 4) "expects PostgreSQL" -> "SQLite (file), Typesense, AI keys".
- [ ] Document ongoing backup = `VACUUM INTO 'snapshot-$(date).db'` (NOT raw cp — unsafe under WAL without `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`).
- [ ] Optional fold-in: bn2 (RSS N+1) is independent and can land anytime.

- lib/pq STAYS through the cutover window (Decision D6): models/notifications.go, handlers/schemas.go (pq.Error duplicate-key detection), server/database.go, and the ETL tool all still import it. Removal is Phase 7b, ~2 weeks after confirmed-prod.

Scope (from the design doc Phase 6b):
- New cmd/migrate-pg-to-sqlite/ binary: reads live PG tables via lib/pq, writes SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, in FK-dependency order, preserving PKs verbatim so the graph (entity_card_junction, backlinks, task_dependencies, ...) stays intact.

- Domain tables migrated verbatim (cards, card_tags, entities, entity_card_junction, facts, tasks, files, flashcards, summarizations, chat_*, notifications, user_*, rss_*, emails, audit_events, llm_jobs, llm_query_log, etc. -- full list in design doc). System tables (migrations, schema_definitions) rebuilt by the consolidated schema + migration runner, NOT migrated.

title: Phase 6a: handler pool-vs-test-tx write isolation audit (s.DB vs s.GetDB())
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). Dominant root cause behind the handlers test failures.

Mechanism: handlers.GetDB() returns the rolled-back per-test transaction (h.Server.Tx) in testing mode, but many handler methods write via the raw pool handle s.DB instead, which COMMITS for real. Reads that then go through GetDB() see a snapshot from before the write -> wrong result. Same mechanism leaks rows across tests (test pollution), since pool writes are never rolled back by Teardown.

Concrete confirmed case: handlers/auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute does s.DB.Exec('UPDATE users SET password = ...'). Then LoginRoute -> QueryUserByEmail (handlers/users.go:411) reads via s.GetDB() (the test tx, snapshot taken in Setup before the reset) -> sees the OLD password hash -> checkPasswordHash fails -> 401. TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess fails on SQLite; on Postgres MVCC the same staleness applies but the suite may have masked it by ordering. Other handlers using raw s.DB.Exec/Query (auth.go:352/383/413/449/475, plus JobRunner wired with S.DB in handlers/setup_test.go) are suspect.

Knock-on pollution (tests that pass in isolation but fail in the full suite because earlier pool-writes leak): TestGetRelatedCards_Success, TestCreateCardLinkedParentId, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags, and the 'database is locked' cleanup in TestGetNextChildCardID (pool write during an open tx).

Fix is a systematic audit, NOT a one-line change: route handler writes through GetDB() everywhere a test tx exists; reserve raw s.DB for the few places that genuinely need out-of-transaction access (and make them explicit). Source/JobRunner wiring (setup_test.go) should pass GetDB() too. Verify isolation holds by running the full handlers package (not just single tests).

File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a. Largest lever among the remaining failures (~4-5 of the 11).
acceptance_criteria: No handler write path uses raw s.DB where a test-transaction-aware GetDB() is intended; TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess green on SQLite; cross-test card/prefs leakage (Typesense upsert of card 28, etc.) eliminated; documented convention for when raw pool access is legitimately required.
notes:
PART 1 LANDED 2026-07-27 (commit pending): routed two handler write paths through GetDB(): auth.go:197 ResetPasswordRoute (was s.DB.Exec UPDATE users password; the auth-reset test failed because the login read via s.GetDB()/tx couldn't see the pool-committed write) -- fixes TestAuthResetPasswordAndLoginSuccess. entity.go: all 13 s.DB method-call sites -> s.GetDB() (the entity-card junction INSERT/DELETE/UPDATE writes were the prime pollution suspect for TestGetRelatedCards_Success; reads converted too for consistency). 2 sites kept as s.DB (GetEntities, NewDefaultClient) because their service signatures take *sql.DB, not the interface -- they are reads and don't pollute. Net: handlers failures 8 -> 7, no regressions.

ROOT-CAUSE FINDING (the rest of bto): converting handler WRITES alone is insufficient. The codebase has pervasive s.DB vs s.GetDB() handle INCONSISTENCY in TWO places that must be fixed TOGETHER:
1. TEST LAYER: cards_test.go has 15 sites calling services.CreateCard/UpdateCard(s.DB, ...) directly with the POOL (lines 617,630,742,754,766,778,790,839,851,906,925,938,950,963,994). CreateCard/UpdateCard do all the entity/backlink/fact writes, so pool calls COMMIT and leak across tests (test data is seeded once via sync.Once; pool writes accumulate). This is the source of TestGetRelatedCards_Success pollution (entity_card_junction deletions accumulate until card 1 has no shared entities) AND TestGetNextChildCardID nondeterminism.
2. HANDLER READ PATH: several reads use s.DB (pool), e.g. getNextChildCardID mixes handles within one function -- parent via s.GetDB() (tx) but children via services.GetChildCards(s.DB, ...) (pool). Converting ONLY the test layer breaks: a tx-local create becomes invisible to pool reads (regression observed: TestCheckChunkLinkedOrRelated_Integration broke when only tests were converted).

CORRECT FIX (part 2): convert BOTH together -- all remaining handler s.DB reads+writes to s.GetDB() (the ~80-site audit, minus legitimately-pool-only paths: Stripe webhooks in billing.go, OAuth callbacks in oauth.go, fire-and-forget last_login/last_seen) AND the 15 test-layer services.*(s.DB) calls. Verified directionally that this works but the full sweep needs care (scheduler/background paths where Server.Testing=true but no request tx exists are the risk). Recommend doing it file-by-file with the full suite as the gate.

NOT FIXED YET: TestGetRelatedCards_Success (pollution), TestGetNextChildCardID (handle-mix). The 2 stale status-code expectations (TestCreateCardLinkedParentId GET-expects-201, TestCreateCardSuccessRecursiveTags expects-200-route-returns-201) and 3 RSS network-dependent tests are SEPARATE pre-existing issues, not bto.

title: Phase 6a: notification_preferences UPDATE is not an upsert (relies on a trigger that never existed)
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a root-cause analysis (2026-07-26). handlers/notifications.go UpdatePreferences (line ~236) contains the comment 'This is handled by the trigger in the database' — but NO such trigger exists. Migration 0121 only runs a one-time INSERT INTO notification_preferences (user_id) SELECT id FROM users ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; there is no per-user auto-create trigger, and it was never ported to Go in Phase 5 (Phase 5 covered user_stats / llm_jobs / rss notifications, not this).

Consequence: models.UpdateNotificationPreferences does a plain UPDATE ... WHERE user_id = $1. When the user has no prefs row (common — e.g. test users inserted by importTestData, or any user created after the 0121 backfill), the UPDATE affects 0 rows, the handler's 'no rows' retry branch never fires (Exec returns no error), and the subsequent GetNotificationPreferences returns 'sql: no rows' -> handler returns 500 'Failed to get preferences'. This is a latent bug on BOTH Postgres and SQLite, not a SQLite regression.

Fix: make models.UpdateNotificationPreferences an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET ... (works identically on both drivers; the table PK is user_id). Drop the misleading trigger comment and the dead retry branch.

TestUpdatePreferencesSuccess is the failing test. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.

title: Phase 6a follow-up: port handlers/facts.go + handlers/entity.go = ANY($1) + array_position to SQLite
description:
Surfaced during Phase 6a (2026-07-26). Two production handler sites still use the Postgres array pattern that the services layer was fixed for in the same session:

- handlers/facts.go:808 -- WHERE f.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, f.id), called with pq.Array(factIDs)
- handlers/entity.go:1141 -- WHERE e.id = ANY($1) ORDER BY array_position($1, e.id), called with pq.Array(entityIDs)

The other 7 '= ANY($1)' sites were translated to IN (...) via the new models.InList / models.IntArgs helpers (models/sql.go). These 2 were deferred because they ALSO use 'ORDER BY array_position($1, col)' to preserve the input-slice order, which SQLite has no equivalent for.

Fix: translate '= ANY($1)' to 'IN ' || models.InList(1, len(ids)) (no fixed scalars here, so start at 1), drop the ORDER BY array_position clause, bind via models.IntArgs(ids)..., then reorder the scanned rows app-side to match the input ids order (collect into a map[id]row, emit in input order). Drop the lib/pq import from both files. Verify on both drivers.

These currently fail at runtime on SQLite with 'no such function: ANY' / 'no such function: array_position', contributing to TestGetRelatedCards_Success and the fact-link handler failures. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j, Phase 6a.

title: Generalize SQLite incremental schema migrations beyond the hand-maintained self-heal list
description: Surfaced by the 2026-08-04 OIDC prod outage ('no such column: oidc_provider'). The SQLite migration path only applies the consolidated schema/sqlite/schema.sqlite.sql for FRESH builds; the numbered Postgres migrations in ./schema (e.g. 0147-add-oidc-subject.sql) are never scanned on SQLite and use non-portable syntax (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, COMMENT ON) anyway. So existing/pre-cutover SQLite DBs had no way to pick up new columns except a manual ALTER. Immediate fix landed (commit pending): server/database.go ensureSQLiteSchemaUpgrades() runs idempotently on every boot and back-fills the oidc_provider/oidc_sub columns + idx_users_oidc_sub index, guarded by table/column-existence checks. Remaining work (this issue): replace the hand-maintained upgrade list with a real incremental-migration mechanism for SQLite — e.g. a SQLite-specific migrations subdir scanned by RunMigrations containing idempotent, SQLite-safe statements, or a small framework that guards each ALTER. Until then, any new NOT-NULL-on-add or type-change column (which SQLite ADD COLUMN can't express) would need a rebuild or a one-off. Design ref: docs/plans/2026-08-03-oidc-authentication-design.md Database/Schema section.

title: Phase 5 follow-up: harden userstats addAmount $2-twice param reuse against driver version bumps
description:
Follow-up from the Phase 5 review (2026-07-26). services/userstats.go addAmount() references $2 twice in one statement (once in VALUES, once in the ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET) and binds a single positional arg. modernc.org/sqlite v1.54.0 and lib/pq both correctly bind the same arg to both occurrences (verified by services/userstats_sqlite_test.go which accumulates to ~0.20 llm_cost / 750 revenue), so this works today on both drivers.

The concern is purely future-proofing: reuse of a numbered param is the one construct in the SQLite migration that is most sensitive to a modernc version bump changing how repeated numbered params are bound.

Options if it ever breaks (low priority): (a) bind the amount twice from the caller side ($2 and $3), or (b) switch to a named param via sql.Named. No action needed today -- this issue exists purely as a breadcrumb so a future 'user_stats add failed' after a go.mod bump is diagnosable in seconds.

Not a blocker for anything. File under epic Zettelgarden-c7j.
